questions.q: A 35-year-old man from rural India presents with a hypopigmented patch on the left cheek that has been present for 6 months. On examination, the patch is anaesthetic with absent sweating. Slit-skin smear shows no acid-fast bacilli. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Indeterminate leprosy presents as a single hypopigmented macule with sensory loss in early disease; slit-skin smear is negative. It may evolve into any type of leprosy.

questions.q: A 28-year-old HIV-positive man develops multiple painful nodular lesions over the face and trunk. Biopsy shows spindle cells with slit-like vascular spaces and extravasated red blood cells. CD4 count is 80 cells/µL. The causative organism is:
questions.exp: Kaposi's sarcoma in immunocompromised patients is caused by Human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8). It presents with violaceous nodules and histology shows spindle cells with vascular slits.

questions.q: A 22-year-old woman presents with recurrent episodes of fluid-filled blisters predominantly on the dorsum of hands and feet. Biopsy shows subepidermal blister with eosinophils. Direct immunofluorescence reveals linear IgA deposits at the basement membrane zone. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Linear IgA disease shows linear IgA deposits at the BMZ on DIF. It differs from DIF of BP (IgG + C3) and DH (IgA in dermal papillae). Clinically it presents with tense blisters in a 'cluster of jewels' pattern.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with a 3-year history of symmetrical non-scarring alopecia with diffuse hair loss. Blood tests show TSH 8.5 mIU/L and anti-TPO antibodies positive. The most appropriate first-line treatment is:
questions.exp: This patient has hypothyroidism-induced diffuse hair loss (telogen effluvium). Treating the underlying thyroid disorder with levothyroxine is the definitive first-line approach.

questions.q: A 30-year-old sexually active man presents with a painless genital ulcer with clean base and indurated edges. VDRL is reactive 1:8. The drug of choice for primary syphilis is:
opts: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM single dose
questions.exp: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM as a single dose is the WHO and IADVL recommended first-line treatment for primary, secondary, and early latent syphilis.

questions.q: A 50-year-old farmer presents with a verrucous plaque on the foot with black dots on the surface ('sclerotic bodies'). KOH mount shows brown, thick-walled muriform cells with horizontal and vertical septa. The most appropriate treatment is:
questions.exp: Chromoblastomycosis (caused by Fonsecaea, Phialophora, Cladosporium spp.) is treated with itraconazole 200–400 mg/day. The characteristic finding is muriform (sclerotic) bodies in tissue.

questions.q: A 16-year-old presents with comedones, papules, and pustules on the face. A few lesions on the chest are also noted. Which sebaceous gland change is the initial event in acne pathogenesis?
questions.exp: Follicular hyperkeratinisation (abnormal desquamation of the follicular infundibulum) is the first step in microcomedone formation in acne vulgaris.

questions.q: A 40-year-old woman presents with butterfly-shaped erythema over the cheeks sparing the nasolabial folds, oral ulcers, and joint pain. ANA titre is 1:320 (speckled pattern). Anti-dsDNA antibody is strongly positive. The most specific antibody for this condition is:
questions.exp: Anti-Sm (anti-Smith) antibody is highly specific for SLE (specificity ~99%) though sensitivity is low (~25%). Anti-dsDNA is both specific and sensitive; anti-Sm is the most specific.

questions.q: A 55-year-old man on long-term treatment for rheumatoid arthritis develops silvery-white plaques with well-defined borders over the elbows and knees, with nail pitting. Which drug he is taking is known to EXACERBATE this condition?
questions.exp: Antimalarials (hydroxychloroquine, chloroquine) can exacerbate psoriasis. Beta-blockers, lithium, and NSAIDs are also known to worsen psoriasis.

questions.q: A 60-year-old man presents with a pearly, translucent nodule on the nose with telangiectasias on the surface. He is a farmer with extensive sun exposure. The most common type of skin cancer in India is:
questions.exp: Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) is the most common skin cancer worldwide and in India, especially on sun-exposed areas like the nose. It has a pearly, rolled border with telangiectasias.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman develops a generalised maculopapular rash 10 days after starting amoxicillin-clavulanate. She has fever and lymphadenopathy. Monospot test is positive. The drug reaction in this case is best classified as:
opts: Viral exanthem unrelated to the drug
questions.exp: Ampicillin/amoxicillin causes a characteristic maculopapular rash in nearly 100% of patients with infectious mononucleosis (EBV). This is a drug-virus interaction, not a true allergy.

questions.q: A 35-year-old presents with target lesions with dusky centres, erosions of the mouth, and involvement of less than 10% BSA following herpes simplex virus reactivation. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Erythema multiforme major involves >1 mucous membrane with typical target lesions and is most commonly triggered by HSV. SJS involves <10% BSA detachment but with atypical targets; EM major preserves typical targets.

questions.q: A 45-year-old diabetic woman presents with satellite lesions around a central erythematous patch in the inframammary fold. KOH examination shows pseudohyphae and budding yeast. The treatment of choice is:
questions.exp: Candida intertrigo is treated with topical imidazoles (clotrimazole, miconazole). The characteristic satellite pustules and pseudohyphae on KOH confirm Candida.

questions.q: A 20-year-old presents with intense pruritus worse at night, involving the finger webs, wrist flexures, and genitals. Several family members are similarly affected. What is the pathognomonic finding in this condition?
questions.exp: Burrows (linear or S-shaped tunnels) created by the female Sarcoptes scabiei mite are pathognomonic for scabies. They are most prominent in finger webs and wrist flexures.

questions.q: A 40-year-old man presents with violaceous flat-topped papules on the wrists and oral white lacy patches (Wickham's striae). Histology shows 'saw-tooth' rete ridges with basal cell liquefaction and a dense lymphocytic band at the DEJ. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Lichen planus shows the 5 Ps (pruritic, purple, polygonal, planar, papules) and Wickham's striae on mucosa. Histology: saw-tooth rete ridges, band-like lymphocytic infiltrate, and Max-Joseph spaces.

questions.q: A 30-year-old pregnant woman develops a pruritic urticarial papule and plaque rash on the abdomen starting in the striae distensae at 36 weeks of gestation. The umbilicus is characteristically spared. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: PUPP (polymorphic eruption of pregnancy) begins in abdominal striae with characteristic umbilical sparing. Pemphigoid gestationis typically involves the umbilicus and shows periumbilical blistering.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman presents with hardening of skin on the hands and face, Raynaud's phenomenon, and dysphagia. Scl-70 antibody is positive. The most specific antibody for diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis is:
questions.exp: Anti-Scl-70 (anti-topoisomerase I) antibody is specific for diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis with higher risk of interstitial lung disease. Anti-centromere antibody is associated with limited cutaneous (CREST) form.

questions.q: A 28-year-old presents with a painless, soft, non-tender genital ulcer with undermined edges and an inguinal bubo that is becoming fluctuant. Gram stain shows school of fish pattern with gram-negative rods. The diagnosis and treatment are:
questions.exp: Chancroid (Haemophilus ducreyi) presents with a painful ulcer with undermined edges and tender inguinal lymphadenopathy (bubo). Gram stain shows school of fish pattern. Azithromycin 1 g single dose is the first-line treatment.

questions.q: A 65-year-old presents with a verrucous plaque at the lower leg margin. Biopsy shows epidermal hyperplasia with horn pearls and individual cell dyskeratosis without basement membrane breach. There is moderate cellular atypia. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Bowen's disease (SCC in-situ) shows full-thickness epidermal dysplasia with atypical cells, horn pearls, dyskeratosis, but the basement membrane is intact. It presents as a persistent erythematous scaly plaque.

questions.q: A 10-year-old child from Bihar presents with hypopigmented macules on the trunk with fine bran-like scales. Wood's lamp examination shows yellow-green fluorescence. KOH examination shows 'spaghetti and meatballs' appearance. The causative organism is:
questions.exp: Pityriasis versicolor is caused by Malassezia furfur (Pityrosporum orbiculare). KOH shows short hyphae and round spores ('spaghetti and meatballs'). Wood's lamp: yellow-green fluorescence in hypopigmented lesions.

questions.q: A 70-year-old man presents with grouped vesicles along the right T5 dermatome associated with severe burning pain. The most feared complication is:
questions.exp: Post-herpetic neuralgia (PHN) is the most common complication of herpes zoster, especially in elderly patients. It is defined as pain persisting beyond 3 months after healing of the rash.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman on dapsone for dermatitis herpetiformis develops acute haemolytic anaemia with methaemoglobinaemia. The G6PD enzyme level is normal. The most appropriate management is:
opts: Reduce dapsone dose and add cimetidine
questions.exp: Dapsone-induced haemolysis and methaemoglobinaemia occur even with normal G6PD. Reducing the dose and adding cimetidine (which inhibits dapsone hydroxylation via CYP2C9) can reduce toxicity while maintaining efficacy.

questions.q: A 32-year-old presents with widespread flushing, pruritus, and urticaria after ingesting aspirin. No respiratory compromise. Skin prick test to aspirin is negative. The most likely mechanism is:
opts: Aspirin-exacerbated cutaneous disease via COX-1 inhibition
questions.exp: Aspirin-exacerbated cutaneous disease (AECD) results from COX-1 inhibition increasing leukotriene synthesis, causing urticaria/angioedema without IgE involvement. Skin prick test is negative.

questions.q: A 45-year-old presents with woody induration of the skin of the lower legs with hyperpigmentation and varicose veins. There is no pitting oedema. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Lipodermatosclerosis is a fibrosis of the subcutaneous fat due to chronic venous insufficiency, presenting with woody induration, hyperpigmentation, and inverted champagne bottle appearance on the lower legs.

questions.q: A 60-year-old woman is on long-term hydroxychloroquine for SLE. Which ophthalmological complication must be monitored?
questions.exp: Hydroxychloroquine (and chloroquine) can cause irreversible retinal toxicity (bull's eye maculopathy). Annual ophthalmological screening with OCT is recommended for patients on long-term therapy.

questions.q: A 22-year-old man presents with multiple grouped follicular papules and pustules on the beard area that do not improve with antibiotics. Fungal culture grows dermatophytes. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Tinea barbae is a dermatophyte infection of the beard area, presenting with follicular papules/pustules not responding to antibiotics. Culture and KOH confirm the fungal aetiology. Treated with oral terbinafine.

questions.q: During patch testing for contact dermatitis, when is the final reading done to confirm delayed hypersensitivity reactions?
questions.exp: Patch tests are applied for 48 hours and readings are done at 48 hours (patch removal) and again at 72–96 hours. The 72–96 hour reading is definitive for Type IV delayed hypersensitivity reactions.

questions.q: A 35-year-old presents with a painful nodule on the palm that has been growing for 6 months. Excision biopsy shows infiltrating bundles of spindle cells producing collagen, with low mitotic activity. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans (DFSP) is a low-grade fibrohistiocytic tumour with infiltrating spindle cells in a storiform pattern. CD34 positive on immunostaining. Wide local excision is recommended.

questions.q: A 28-year-old presents with exquisitely pruritic vesicles on extensor surfaces of elbows, knees, and buttocks. IgA deposits are found in the dermal papillae on DIF. The associated systemic condition is:
questions.exp: Dermatitis herpetiformis (DH) is closely associated with gluten-sensitive enteropathy (coeliac disease). DIF shows granular IgA deposits in dermal papillae. Dapsone and gluten-free diet are first-line treatments.

questions.q: A 50-year-old woman presents with multiple flesh-coloured, firm papules on the neck and axillae that are soft and pedunculated. Some are hyperpigmented. The term for these benign skin tags is:
questions.exp: Acrochordons (skin tags, fibroepithelial polyps) are benign, soft, pedunculated, flesh-coloured papules commonly occurring in skin folds. They are associated with obesity, diabetes, and acanthosis nigricans.

questions.q: A 40-year-old man presents with erythematous plaques on the face that appear after brief sun exposure and resolve within hours without residual change. ANA is 1:80 (speckled), anti-Ro positive. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus (SCLE) is photosensitive, presents with annular or papulosquamous lesions triggered by UV, heals without scarring, and is strongly associated with anti-Ro/SSA antibodies.
